runs.t: PACELC extends CAP: if partitioned, choose between availability and consistency; else, even in normal operation, choose between latency and consistency. It captures everyday cost of coordination.

A strongly consistent cross-region read may require waiting for remote coordination, while a local replica responds faster with possible staleness. Record per-operation consistency and latency objectives rather than naming a database category.
An international product catalog may read nearby replicas for speed, while inventory reservation routes through a leader or quorum to prevent double allocation.
PACELC is a heuristic, not a complete specification of real systems. Topology, caches, quorum settings and failure detection affect observed behavior; benchmark realistic networks.
